guarantees.claim: fifo_rready_o is sha_rready_i when hmac_en_i is low; when hmac_en_i is high, it is (st_q == StMsg) & sha_rready_i.
sha_rvalid_o equals fifo_rvalid_i when hmac_en_i is low; otherwise equals hmac_sha_rvalid.

sha_rdata_o outputs fifo_rdata_i when hmac_en_i low or when sel_rdata is not SelIPad/SelOPad; for SelIPad with SHA2_256, it outputs i_pad_256 slice with mask all-ones; for SelIPad with SHA2_384/512, i_pad_512 slice with mask all-ones; for SelOPad with SHA2_256, o_pad_256 slice with mask all-ones; for SelOPad with SHA2_384/512, o_pad_512 slice with mask all-ones.
When sha_rdata_o outputs a pad slice (ipad/opad conditions true), the mask field is driven to all-ones, exposing the full 32-bit data word.

assumptions.claim: sel_rdata is always a legal enum value (SelIPad, SelOPad, SelFifo) and never the illegal 2'b11.
assumptions.cond: when hmac_en_i is high and sel_rdata controls sha_rdata_o mux
assumptions.risk: An illegal sel_rdata would hit the default case and output fifo_rdata_i, potentially leaking internal FIFO data or corrupting the HMAC data path.

assumptions.claim: digest_size_i is restricted to SHA2_256, SHA2_384, or SHA2_512 when sel_rdata is SelIPad or SelOPad.
assumptions.cond: when hmac_en_i high and pad mux conditions are evaluated
assumptions.risk: An unsupported digest size would not match any pad condition, causing the default fifo_rdata_i to be selected, which would break HMAC operation and potentially leak message data.

assumptions.claim: pad_index_256 and pad_index_512 are always within the bounds of the i_pad_256/o_pad_256 and i_pad_512/o_pad_512 arrays respectively.
assumptions.cond: when the corresponding pad slice is selected
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds indexing would read undefined data, causing X propagation or functional failure in the HMAC hash operation.

uncertain_points.claim: If digest_size_i takes a value other than SHA2_256/384/512 while sel_rdata is SelIPad or SelOPad, the mux silently falls back to fifo_rdata_i instead of providing the correct pad data.
uncertain_points.cond: hmac_en_i high, sel_rdata == SelIPad/SelOPad, digest_size_i not in {SHA2_256, SHA2_384, SHA2_512}
uncertain_points.risk: This would cause the HMAC to use incorrect padding data, leading to wrong MAC computation or potential security bypass. Need to verify that digest_size_i is always constrained to the covered set.

uncertain_points.claim: When outputting ipad/opad data, the mask field is set to all-ones, exposing the entire 32-bit pad word. The pad data is derived from the HMAC key and may be secret.
uncertain_points.risk: If this sha_rdata_o bus is observable (e.g., to a core or debug interface) or later written to memory without further masking, the secret key material could be leaked. Need to confirm whether this exposure is intentional and contained within the crypto boundary.

uncertain_points.claim: The comment states that sel_rdata == 2'b11 cannot occur, but it is unclear if external FSMs or configuration registers guarantee this restriction. The default case would output fifo_rdata_i, which might be harmless or could leak internal state depending on the overall dataflow.
uncertain_points.risk: If sel_rdata is not fully constrained elsewhere, an attacker or fault could inject this value and cause unexpected data exposure or functional corruption.
